summary.text: 学 is used for learning and study today. It is the standardized simplified counterpart of 學; its visible parts do not settle the traditional graph’s disputed early construction.

formation.text: The current graph 学 is arranged ⿳⺍冖子: ⺍ and 冖 form an upper assembly above 子. This visible split does not settle how traditional 學 was first constructed. One account interprets oracle-bone forms as 𦥑 (two hands) with 五 and 六, while allowing that 爻 may supply a sound cue in some forms. Separate proposals describe phonosemantic forms with 爻 as sound and 冖 as the other element; a rare, unidentified element read jù and depicted as hands or claws; and a distinct construction grouping two 臼 forms with 冖 and a following unidentified graphic unit assigned the sound role. The two 臼 shapes may be reduced to person-like forms; this reduction does not apply to 冖. The rare jù account is separate from the two-臼 proposal. These are competing interpretations, not a settled reconstruction. One source also proposes learning and emulation as 學’s original meaning, but the proposal is unsettled. The modern simplified shape does not establish the ancient structure.

components.text: This is the visible top part of the upper assembly in 学’s ⿳⺍冖子 arrangement. No historical, semantic, or phonetic function is established for it.
冖 is the visible middle component below ⺍ and above 子 in 学. Its identity here does not establish a roof meaning or an ancient role.
子 is the visible lower component of 学; the evidence does not establish its present-day function in this graph.

history.text: 學 is the traditional counterpart of standardized simplified 学. The graphic path from early forms to either modern shape is not established here.

A later lexicographic account describes 學 as an abbreviated seal-script form of 斆, which it analyzes as 教 and 冖 with 𦥑 supplying the sound. This received account does not confirm the structure of earlier forms.

uncertainties.text: The early construction accounts remain distinct. One interprets some forms as 𦥑 (two hands) with tally-like elements 五 and 六, while allowing that 爻 may supply a sound cue in some forms. Other proposals describe phonosemantic forms with 爻 as sound and 冖 as the other element; a separate, unusual element read jù and depicted as hands or claws; and a distinct construction grouping two 臼 forms with 冖 and a following unidentified graphic unit assigned the sound role. The two 臼 shapes may be reduced to person-like forms; this does not apply to 冖, and the rare jù element is not identified as 臼. These proposals do not establish one construction for every early form. The claim that 學’s original meaning was learning and emulation is a proposal, not an established conclusion.
The graphic path from early 學 forms to 学 is unresolved. The modern top alone does not establish an ancient roof component or a specific corruption.
An oracle-bone occurrence is reported, but its archaeological date and context are not specified beyond that identification.

senses.text: 學 and its standardized simplified counterpart 学 are currently used for learning and study.

senses.period: current; school use attested for 學 in bronze inscriptions
senses.text: Traditional 學 is reported in bronze inscriptions in a school context. In present-day compounds such as 小學、中學 and 大學, 學—and its standardized simplified counterpart 学—is a morpheme naming an educational institution or place of learning; these examples do not establish 学 as a standalone word meaning “school.” The evidence does not establish when the school use began.
A bronze-inscription example uses traditional 學 in a passage about archery instruction. This evidence does not establish a full semantic sequence from learning to teaching.
The Qin-slip phrase 成學 is reported with the meaning “complete one’s studies”; it illustrates a contextual use of traditional 學.

senses.gloss: feel; perceive, written with the graph 學
senses.text: A source reports traditional 學 used in Han slips as a borrowed spelling for 覺, “feel” or “perceive.” The reason for choosing this spelling is not established. This is a reported spelling loan, not a meaning that developed from “learning.”

limitations.text: The bronze examples report school and instruction uses for 學, while current dictionary examples show 学 in school-related compounds. These period-separated examples do not establish a full sequence among learning, school, and instruction.
A source reports traditional 學 used as a borrowed spelling for 覺 (“feel”); the reason for choosing that spelling is not explained in the cited report.

overview.text: 学 means learning or study and is the standardized simplified counterpart of 學. Its visible upper assembly, ⺍ over 冖, sits above 子; these current parts do not settle the ancient construction.

components.text: ⺍ is the top subpart of 学’s upper assembly, with 冖 below it; the assembly’s function is unresolved.
冖 is the middle part of 学’s upper assembly; its shape alone does not establish a roof meaning or ancient role here.
子 is visible in 学. One proposal says it was added to 學 in Western Zhou forms to mark a child learner; its present-day function remains unresolved.

limitations.text: The only candidate is a modern vector redraw labeled in oracle-script style; it is not a verified historical specimen. Its pixels do not establish a catalogued glyph or resolve the competing accounts of 學’s early construction, so it cannot support a useful historical-form comparison here.
